name: writeDataToFirebase
summary: Google Apps Script routine that reads every row of the first sheet of a spreadsheet and writes it into a Firebase Realtime Database node as an object keyed by one of the columns, turning a hand-maintained sheet into an app-readable dataset.
details: The answer to "have I ever pushed a Google Sheet into Firebase?". Mechanism: getDataRange().getValues() reads the whole sheet in one call, the loop starts at index 1 to skip the header row, and rows are collected into a plain object keyed by the name column rather than an array — so the RTDB node is a map, lookups are by name, and re-running overwrites rather than appends. base.setData("beers", ...) replaces the entire node each run; there is no merge and no delete detection beyond that. Column indexes are hard-coded positional (data[i][1] name, [2] country, [3] type, [4] style, [6] places), so inserting a column silently corrupts the export. Depends on the third-party FirebaseApp Apps Script library (FirebaseApp.getDatabaseByUrl), which must be added to the script project by library id; that dependency is invisible in the source and is the thing that stops a copy-paste of this file from running. The spreadsheet id and database URL are placeholdered (YOUR_GOOGLE_SHEET_ID, YOUR_FIREBASE_DATABSE_URL - typo in the original), and the data being exported is a personal beer catalogue.
